record.title: OpenAI sets prior review for direct model-access intermediaries and restricts substitute-model training uses
record.summary: On October 21, OpenAI published Usage Policy changes effective November 20, 2026. They require prior OpenAI review and approval for model-access intermediary platforms or other services that enable third parties to directly access OpenAI models; an application is not covered solely because it integrates OpenAI models into its own features. The policy also bars using OpenAI models or outputs to prepare training materials or signals for models intended as alternatives or substitutes, subject to uses expressly permitted by an applicable agreement. These are stated policy terms; implementation and market effects remain unobserved.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI's Usage Policies dated October 21 state that, effective November 20, 2026, a model-access intermediary platform or other service enabling third parties to directly access OpenAI models must obtain prior review and approval; merely integrating models into an application is not sufficient to trigger this rule.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The updated policy prohibits using OpenAI models or outputs to prepare training materials or signals for models intended as alternatives or substitutes for OpenAI models or services, while preserving uses expressly permitted by the applicable agreement.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The policy text does not establish how many providers will seek approval, how approvals will be administered, whether services will change, or what economic effects will follow.

evidence_gaps.description: The announced terms take effect November 20, 2026; operational review processes, affected services, approvals and enforcement have not been observed.
No evidence in the inspected sources quantifies affected intermediaries or measures market, access, or model-development effects.

brief.importance_rationale: If effective as stated, prior review for services that directly expose OpenAI models and restrictions on using outputs to train substitute models can change distribution and model-development options for affected providers. The scope is limited to OpenAI services and applicable agreements; no implementation, affected-provider counts, or economic effects have been observed.
limitations: The sources are OpenAI's own policy and explanation; they establish the announced terms, not independent assessment or implementation.
The policy text includes agreement-specific permitted exceptions; the record does not determine individual customer contracts.
No affected-provider count, approval outcome, enforcement evidence, or measured economic impact was located.

technical.claimed_result: OpenAI announces a prior-review requirement for services that directly provide third parties access to its models and restrictions on using OpenAI outputs to prepare substitute-model training material or signals.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official policy pages document the stated rules, scope clarification, agreement exception and November 20, 2026 effective date. They do not demonstrate implementation or economic outcomes.
technical.mechanism: Policy terms condition direct model-access intermediary services on prior OpenAI review and approval and prohibit specified substitute-model training uses of OpenAI models or outputs, subject to applicable agreement exceptions.
technical.regime: OpenAI Usage Policies governing use of OpenAI services, announced October 21, 2026 and scheduled to take effect November 20, 2026.
technical.strongest_baseline: The previous Usage Policies version linked by OpenAI; a clause-by-clause comparison was not performed in this activation.

brief.title: OpenAI sets prior review for direct model-access intermediaries and restricts substitute-model training uses
brief.why_it_matters: The changes set new stated conditions for direct third-party access to OpenAI models and constrain some uses of OpenAI outputs in substitute-model development. If applied as written, they could affect intermediary service design and model-training workflows, but the source does not establish the number of affected providers or any realized economic effect.
